perQuestion.answer: The project avoided frequent re-centering (narrowing) because the 720-day backtests showed the extra fees were more than offset by impermanent loss (IL) from rebalancing. In the flat regime, where narrowing should theoretically win, the passive wide range still outperformed (e.g., 86% vs 59% win rate on cbBTC).

We FLAT wszystko wygrywa: adapt k3h24 100%wygr/najgorsze +2.66
fees do not cover LVR

perQuestion.answer: The project did not find that LPs earned less in fees during uptrends; the opposite was true. Narrow positions collected the most fees in volatile/trending windows (e.g., "$2.7–5.3k"), but those fees were wiped out by realized IL/LVR and rotation costs, producing the worst net results. In flat markets, the same or wider positions kept IL low and fees positive, so they beat HODL. Thus, fee income was not lower in uptrends; the net edge was lower because trend-driven losses exceeded the extra fees.

perQuestion.answer: FLAT_NARROW is a proposal kind (an action), not a specific position or a range algorithm. The bot emits it when a flat is confirmed (|gap|<2% for ≥12h) to narrow the position from a wide band (e.g., ±40%) to a fixed product width (e.g., ±5%). The width comes from a product config field (productNarrowWidthPct) or, previously, a k×σ advisor; the range is computed via suggestFixedRange. It is paired with FLAT_WIDEN (widen back after flat ends).

citations.quote: factory.getPool → slot0 + liquidity → nowy Pool z tymi samymi tokenami/fee
fail-open (zwraca stary pool, gdy fabryka/RPC zawiedzie)
wpięty w useRebalanceExecution i useRotateExecution tuż przed buildMintStep
ticki zakresu nadal z planu (liczone przy starym kursie)

perQuestion.answer: fetchFreshPool (in src/utils/uniswap.ts) refreshes pool state before executing a mint: it calls factory.getPool, reads slot0 and liquidity, and constructs a new Pool object with the same tokens and fee tier. It is fail-open—if the factory or RPC call fails, it returns the old pool object instead of throwing. It is wired into useRebalanceExecution and useRotateExecution immediately before buildMintStep. A known caveat: the range ticks still come from the plan (computed at the old price), so after a price move the range is slightly off-center, which is negligible for ±40/50% ranges but can slightly increase post-mint dust.
